solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: May tease surprisingly gullible type

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters of May tease have turned out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Someone called May teases a person who falls for anything, and is surprised by it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone easily fooled or beaten is an easy target, a soft victim for any trickster.

clue.text: Summon over to North London station

indicators.note: over means the word for summon is turned over, read backwards in a down answer

parts.note: to sue someone is to summon them to court
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is ordered to come across to a station in north London.
explanation.walkthrough: Euston is a main-line railway terminus in north London.
explanation.definitionFit: Euston is one of the main railway termini of London.

clue.text: Son unable to appreciate music? Likely, if this

definitions.text: Son unable to appreciate music? Likely, if this

parts.note: someone tone-deaf cannot tell musical notes apart

explanation.surface: A son has no ear for music, which is likely if he cannot hear at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: someone wholly unable to hear would surely be unable to enjoy music.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone completely unable to hear is utterly deaf, and so certainly cannot enjoy any tune.

clue.text: I won't utter a word in Emerald Isle, say, troubled about onset of power-sharing

indicators.note: about means the stirred-up letters surround the next piece
troubled suggests the letters of Emerald Isle, say are stirred up and disordered
onset of points to the first letter of power-sharing

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to comment on troubled Ireland at the start of a power-sharing deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' turns EMERALDISLESAY into MYLISARESEALED, and 'about' puts the P from 'onset of power-sharing' inside it. The Emerald Isle is Ireland, power-sharing in Northern Ireland making the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A promise to keep a secret, saying the speaker will say nothing about the matter.

clue.text: See 23
Handsome youth, a Spaniard on income support

parts.note: Don is the Spanish title for a gentleman, so a Spaniard
IS is the abbreviation for Income Support, a British welfare benefit

explanation.surface: A good-looking young man from Spain is living on state benefits.
explanation.walkthrough: Income Support is a British state benefit for people on low incomes.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite, and his name is used for any good-looking young man.

clue.text: Use of financial power as a weapon to buck the system?

definitions.text: Use of financial power as a weapon to buck the system?

parts.words: Use of financial power as a weapon to buck the system?
parts.note: a buck is slang for the US currency unit, so a system run by bucks is foreign policy driven by money

explanation.surface: Money is used as a weapon to defy the established order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buck the system' looks like defying it, but buck is the American currency unit: diplomacy by money.
explanation.definitionFit: The term for a foreign policy that uses economic investment and loans to extend a nation's influence abroad.

clue.text: Mad dog male abandoned in New York

indicators.note: in means what remains of the dog goes inside the state abbreviation
abandoned means the letter for male is deserted, left out of the word for dog

parts.note: a mutt is a dog

explanation.surface: A rabid dog is abandoned by its owner in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Crazy or eccentric, as in a nutty professor, is a colloquial synonym for mad.

clue.text: Serving up endless wine is ominous

indicators.note: serving up, in a down answer, means the pieces are presented upwards, read in reverse order
endless means the wine's last letter is cut off

parts.note: retsina is a Greek resinated wine
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pouring out wine without end has an ominous feel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serving up' turns RETSIN plus IS backwards together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something threatening or suggesting evil to come seems ominous, a close synonym.

clue.text: Face pressure in a group

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for pressure goes inside the word for group

parts.note: a sect is a group of followers
P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: Someone encounters peer pressure within a group.
explanation.definitionFit: One side or facet of a problem or building is a face of it.

clue.text: Left on barge with a gloomy expression

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece written on another comes after it

parts.note: a scow is a flat-bottomed barge

explanation.surface: Someone left aboard a barge looks miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: A frown of displeasure or bad temper is a sullen, gloomy look on the face.

clue.text: Is so busy trying to gain weight?

definitions.text: Is so busy trying to gain weight?

parts.words: Is so busy trying to gain weight?
parts.note: the idiom for being overloaded with work is read literally as a diner with a heaped dinner dish, eating to put on pounds

annotation.spelling: HAS A LOT ON ONE'S PLATE

explanation.surface: Someone is so preoccupied with bulking up that they have no time for anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for having many tasks or responsibilities to deal with at once, pictured as a heaped dinner dish.

clue.text: See 11
Foolish person crossing through a deep chasm

indicators.note: crossing means the word for a fool spans over, and so contains, the word for through

parts.note: an ass is a fool
by can mean through, as in 'by means of'

explanation.surface: A silly person walks across, passing through a deep gorge.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottomless pit or gulf is a very deep chasm, as in the abyss of the sea.

clue.text: Leave extremely disreputable character

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters, of disreputable

parts.note: a part is a character played by an actor

explanation.surface: Get away from a thoroughly shady person.
explanation.definitionFit: To go away or set off from a place is to leave it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Old tape playing shows a larval toad

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of old tape being toyed with and moved around

explanation.surface: An old cassette, when played, shows a film of a young toad.
explanation.definitionFit: A pollywog is the larval stage of a frog or toad, living in water before it grows legs.

clue.text: Honest one struggling to win

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters of honest one floundering into disorder

explanation.surface: A decent person battles hard to come out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: In betting, a bet 'on the nose' backs a horse to win only, not to be placed.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing bet on the nose is placed for victory only, not each way.

clue.text: Share with twin, perhaps, at university

parts.note: a twin is one example of a double, a lookalike
up means at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: A student shares rooms with a twin at college.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage, being 'up' means being in residence at a university.
explanation.definitionFit: To double up is to share a room or bed with another person.

clue.text: Unusual of female to strike

parts.note: taken as written
to beat is to strike

explanation.surface: It is odd for a woman to hit someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unconventional or eccentric is out of the ordinary, unusual.

clue.text: Changed course with what sounds like diplomacy

indicators.note: what sounds like says the word for diplomacy is said out loud and heard as a different word

parts.note: tact is diplomacy in dealing with people

explanation.surface: Someone shifted approach with something resembling diplomacy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing boat that turns into the wind to alter direction has changed course.

clue.text: Number two's job to get hold of record

indicators.note: to get hold of means the word for job grips, and so contains, the word for record

parts.note: a duty is a task or job
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: The second-in-command's task is to obtain a record.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the definition as 'Number two is': a second-in-command is the one who stands in.
explanation.definitionFit: A second-in-command, who stands in for the boss, is the number two in an organisation.

clue.text: Note taken from Parisian salesgirl in eating area

indicators.note: taken from means the note is removed from the Paris shopgirl

parts.note: a midinette is a Paris shopgirl or seamstress
mi is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A French shop assistant loses a note in a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinette is a small dining space, an alcove for eating, beside a kitchen.

clue.text: Enjoy taking in a show

indicators.note: taking in means the word for enjoy encloses the letter given by a

parts.note: to revel in something is to enjoy it greatly

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys going to see a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To display or disclose something is to show it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Youth, one dropping ring in Irish river

parts.note: a boy is a youth

indicators.note: dropping means the round letter is let fall out of the word for one

parts.note: taken as written
O is a ring, from its shape

explanation.surface: A boy loses a ring in an Irish river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boyne flows into the Irish Sea north of Dublin; the Battle of the Boyne was fought there in 1690.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boyne is a river in eastern Ireland, famous for the battle of 1690.

clue.text: Early, in reality, this Sinatra ballad

parts.note: young means early in life
at heart means fundamentally, in reality

explanation.surface: Early on, truly, this was a Sinatra song.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank Sinatra had a hit with this song in 1953.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinatra recorded this 1953 hit song, whose title describes a youthful spirit.

clue.text: Form of Chinese on Net, case for translation

indicators.note: for translation suggests the words on Net case must be turned into something else, rearranged

explanation.surface: A Chinese variety found online needs translating.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantonese is the variety of Chinese spoken in Guangzhou and Hong Kong.

clue.text: Enthusiastic centre that is based in hospital department

indicators.note: based in means the pieces are set inside the hospital department

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
the bull is the centre of a target, the bullseye
ie is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: An eager specialist centre is located in a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bubbling over with cheerful energy and excitement is enthusiastic.

clue.text: Make amends an hour after midnight

definitions.meaning: to make up for a wrong you have done
read as two words, the time of one o'clock in the morning

explanation.definitionFit: To expiate a wrong is to make amends; split as two words it is the time one o'clock.

clue.text: Temple of a deity in Pennsylvania

indicators.note: in means the words for a deity sit inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania
a god is a deity

explanation.surface: A temple to a god stands in Pennsylvania.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower used as a Buddhist or Hindu temple in Asia.

clue.text: Exceedingly healthy fine

parts.note: very means exceedingly
well means in good health

explanation.surface: Someone is in excellent health.
explanation.definitionFit: Said as a reply, the phrase means 'all right, agreed', the same as fine.
